Get any table of a fitted model, grid, comparison, test or diagnostics result as a data frame

Source: R/get-data.R
get_results.Rd

get_results() returns the results of an object of this package as data frames. Every fitted model, enumeration grid, model comparison, bootstrap test, starting-value set and diagnostics result holds a set of named tables, and what chooses among them. The sections below list every table name for each kind of object, with what one row is, its columns and the arguments it takes. Many tables also have a verb of their own that takes any object, such as get_entropy(), get_best() or get_tree().

Usage

get_results(x, what = NULL, ...)

Arguments

x

A fitted model, an enumeration grid, a model comparison, a bootstrap test, a starting-value set, a diagnostics result or pooled imputations; or the summary() of a fitted model, of a profile or class grid or of a bootstrap test, which holds the same tables.

what

Which table to return:

  • NULL (default): the object's primary table, the same table as as.data.frame(x) and the first one listed for the object below. A profile or class fit without continuous indicators returns the first of "responses", "ordinal" and "count_means" that it has; a general transition fit (class multilpa_lta) returns "transitions";

  • one table name, matched in full and not by its first letters;

  • "all": every table the object builds by default, as a named list.

...

Arguments of the requested table, named in its entry below and described there or under Table arguments.

Value

For one table, a data frame: the table's entry below gives what one row is and the columns. For what = "all", a named list of data frames in the order of the entries, each built with its default arguments. The list leaves out the tables this object cannot produce (the sequence tables of a fit made without time, for example) and those built only when asked for ("lmr", "recovery", and "group_posteriors" of a fit with fewer than two group classes).

Conditions raised:

  • latents_bad_argument: what is not a table of the object (the message lists the names it has), ... holds an argument the table does not take, or x is not an object of this package;

  • latents_unused_argument (a warning): such an argument, given to a table of a cross-level fit or of a transition or family grid;

  • latents_no_time: a sequence table of a fit made without time;

  • latents_no_local_dependence, latents_no_direct_effects: the table of those terms, for a fit without them;

  • latents_unsupported_noise: the classification errors, BCH weights or residuals of a fit with a noise component.

Tables of a profile, class or transition fit

The tables of a fit from lpa(), lca(), multilpa() or multilca(), with or without membership covariates, and of an lta() fit of class multilpa_transitions (the basic transition model). Any other lta() fit has class multilpa_lta and the tables listed under Tables of the other model families.

"profiles"

The Gaussian measurement model, one row per profile and continuous indicator: profile, indicator, mean, variance, standard_deviation, mean_standard_error, variance_standard_error. Takes scale and data.

"responses"

The categorical measurement model, one row per profile, indicator and category: profile, indicator, category, probability, threshold (qlogis(P(y <= category)), NA for the last category), probability_standard_error. Takes data.

"covariances"

One row per profile and ordered pair of continuous indicators: profile, indicator, indicator_2, covariance (exact zeros off the diagonal under a diagonal structure).

"ordinal", "count_means"

Only for fits with ordinal or count indicators. "ordinal" has one row per profile, indicator and category: profile, indicator, category, probability, location (the profile's location on the indicator's latent scale) and location_standard_error. "count_means" has one row per profile and indicator: profile, indicator, mean, standard_error. Take data.

"local_dependence", "direct_effects"

For fits with those arguments. Local dependence has pair, kind, profile, item_1, category_1, item_2, category_2, probability, independent, ratio, covariance, correlation: a categorical pair has one row per profile and category combination with the joint probability, the product of the marginals (independent) and their ratio; a continuous pair one row per profile with covariance and correlation. Direct effects have one row per effect: indicator, covariate, estimate, standard_error, statistic, p_value, conf_low, conf_high.

"counts"

Effective class sizes (summed posteriors), one row per level and class: level, class, effective_count, effective_proportion.

"model", "information_criteria"

One row describing the fit: dimensions, likelihood, parameter counts, criteria, convergence and boundary status; "information_criteria" has the same columns for every family and takes format and definitions (see Information criteria).

"posteriors"

One row per observation and profile: row, group, profile, posterior, modal. Takes format. Excluded observations keep their rows with NA.

"group_posteriors"

One row per group and group class: group, group_size, log_likelihood, group_class, posterior, modal. Takes format.

"assignments"

One row per observation: the columns the fit was built from (or those of data), profile, group_class where there is one, uncertainty (one minus the posterior of the assigned profile), one posterior_profile_* column per profile, and posterior_noise for a noise fit (profile 0). Takes data and truth; with truth it returns a recovery table (Table arguments). Rows with no observed indicator have NA assignments under drop_empty = TRUE, but keep a group class supported by other rows.

"classification"

One row per level and class: level, class, n_modal, proportion_modal, estimated_n, estimated_proportion, average_posterior, odds_correct_classification (see Classification quality). Takes level.

"average_posteriors"

For the units assigned to each class, their mean posterior for every class: level, assigned_class, class, n_assigned, average_posterior; rows sum to one within an assigned class. Takes level.

"classification_errors", "bch_weights"

The probability that a unit of one true class is assigned to another (level, true_class, assigned_class, probability), and the BCH weights that invert that matrix (level, unit, assigned_class, class, weight). Take level. Marginal over the units on a covariate fit.

"entropy"

One row per level: level, n_classes, n_units, entropy_sum, relative_entropy.

"replication"

One row: the numbers of starts run, screened, converged and failed, and n_best_replicated, the starts within tolerance of the best log likelihood. See get_replication().

"starts"

One row per start: start, log_likelihood, converged, iterations, error, boundary where recorded, and under search = "emEM" kind, stage ("final" or "screened") and screened_log_likelihood.

"residuals"

Bivariate residuals of every indicator pair: profile, indicator_1, indicator_2, kind, observed, expected, residual, effective_n, statistic, df, p_value, p_adjusted. One row per pair and profile, or per pair under by = "overall". Takes data, by and adjust. See Bivariate residuals.

"gaussian_diagnostics"

Only for fits with continuous indicators. One row per Gaussian component: context, profile, gaussian_mass, positive_rows, weight_effective_n, min_variance_ratio, min_standardized_eigenvalue, boundary: how much posterior mass a component carries, how concentrated it is, and how small its variances are relative to the data. Descriptive, with no cutoff and no effect on start selection.

"sequences", "sequence_summary"

Fits with time: the assignments in occasion order (group, group_class, time, profile; takes format) and one row per group class (group_class, groups, observations, mean_length, median_length, shortest, longest, complete, gaps).

"data"

The data the model was fitted to, in input order: the identifier, the occasion, the rescaled weights and the indicators under their original names; not the covariates, so three_step() and r3step() take data.

"profile_probabilities", "stages"

A fit without membership covariates or transitions: one row per group class and profile (group_class, profile, probability, group_class_probability), and one row per estimation stage (stage, group_classes, fixed, log_likelihood, parameters, parameters_with_measurement, converged; two rows for a fit_staged() result).

"coefficients"

A fit with membership covariates (profile_covariates or group_covariates): one row per membership coefficient (level "profile" or "group", outcome, term, parameter, always "logit", estimate); standard errors come from parameter_inference().

"transitions", "initial", "sequence_lengths"

An lta() fit: one row per group class and ordered pair of profiles (group_class, from, to, probability, expected_count, origin_expected_count, supported, stable, estimated, group_class_probability; takes estimated and stable); one row per group class and profile (group_class, profile, probability, prevalence, group_class_probability); one row per group (group, group_class, occasions, observations, complete).

Under sampling weights every population quantity, here and in the grid tables, is weighted: effective and estimated counts and proportions, average posteriors, the odds of correct classification, entropy, classification errors, BCH weights, the criteria and the tree's mass. Modal counts stay unweighted counts of the units of positive weight; a unit of weight zero keeps its row and posteriors but enters no statistic.

Tables of an enumeration grid

A profile or class grid from enumerate_lpa(), enumerate_lca() or enumerate_classes() has the tables below. get_candidates(), get_best(), get_deltas(), get_knees() and get_tree() return them too, and their pages describe the columns one by one.

"candidates"

One row per candidate, failed ones included: candidate, its class counts and model, log likelihood, parameter count, every criterion under both sample-size conventions, both entropies, the AvePP summaries of each level, convergence, boundary, replication, the Gaussian diagnostics, warnings and error. Takes cutoff (default 0.8) for avepp_below; a class with no assigned unit counts as below it. get_candidates() drops the columns empty in every row.

"best"

One row per criterion and sample-size convention, with the converged candidate that has the lowest value. "criteria" is its older name, still in "all".

"classification"

One row per fitted candidate, level and class: candidate, its class counts and model, the columns of a fit's "classification" table and the level's relative_entropy.

"deltas", "knees"

Model-selection evidence, taking using, one criterion of the grid (default "bic_groups"); neither selects a model. "deltas" has one row per candidate, with the decrease in the criterion from the converged candidate with one profile fewer (delta_profile) and with one group class fewer (delta_group_class): positive when this candidate is lower, NA where the neighbour is missing or unconverged. "knees" has one row per line of the grid (along the profiles, the group classes or the parameters), with the candidate furthest below the chord of the line (knee_candidate), a simplified Kneedle rule; a line needs three candidates for a knee and four for stable.

"tree"

The flows of plot_tree(), one row per pair of classes in consecutive rows of a tree, with mass, the share of all units the two classes share (summed over the products of their posteriors). Takes the arguments of plot_tree(): n_group_classes, n_profiles (n_classes on a regression grid), model, candidates, from, to and level (default "individuals").

"lmr"

The Vuong-Lo-Mendell-Rubin and adjusted Lo-Mendell-Rubin tests, one row per pair of converged candidates differing by one profile or one group class at the same structure: direction, null_candidate, alternative_candidate, the alternative's class counts and model, n_units, parameters_added, lr, vlmr_p, adjusted_lr (lr / (1 + 1 / (parameters_added * log(n_units)))), almr_p, reference_mean, reference_sd and note. The reference is a weighted chi-square with the eigenvalues of Vuong's matrix as weights, evaluated by Imhof's method; a pair with a singular information matrix or a boundary candidate keeps its row with NA and the reason in note. Built only when asked for.

A transition grid (enumerate_classes(time = )) or a family grid (enumerate_classes(family = )) has three tables:

"candidates"

One row per candidate, with model, warnings, error and the columns get_candidates() lists for the grid.

"best"

One row: the row of "candidates" with the lowest value of one criterion among the converged candidates. Takes criterion: "bic" (default), "aic" or "bic_individual".

"tree"

As for a profile or class grid. Not in "all".

A regression grid from enumerate_regressions() has:

"fit"

One row per candidate, with the columns get_candidates() lists for a regression grid and note; best_bic is TRUE for the converged candidate with the lowest BIC.

"tree"

As for a profile or class grid, with n_classes in place of n_profiles.

"model"

Not a table: the fitted model of one candidate, chosen with n_classes and n_group_classes (default 1). Not in "all".

The fitted models of the other grids and of a comparison are extracted with get_candidate().

Tables of the other objects

A compare_models() result

"comparison": one row per model, with the columns compare_models() lists. "classification": one row per model, level and class, with the columns of a fit's "classification" table and relative_entropy; only when every model compared is a profile, class, covariate or transition model.

A bootstrap_lrt() result

"test": one row, the test. "replicates": one row per simulated data set.

A starting-value set (starting_values())

"profiles", "responses", "profile_probabilities" and "covariances": the rows of a fit's tables of those names, with the estimates only (no standard errors or thresholds).

A diagnostics() result

"entropy", "classification", "average_posteriors", "residuals" and "replication", each as the table of that name of a fit, and "checks", one row per check (columns in get_checks()). "residuals" exists only for a profile, class or multilpa_transitions fit.

Tables of the other model families

Each family has its own tables; the first is the primary one. Tables with intervals take level (the confidence level, default 0.95) and vcov_type ("observed", "robust" or "opg"; NULL reuses the type stored with a regression fit).

A mixture regression (mixture_regression()):

"coefficients"

One row per class and term: class, term, estimate, std_error, statistic, p_value, conf_low, conf_high, p_adjusted (Benjamini-Hochberg over the non-intercepts) and, where the link makes it an odds or rate ratio, exp_estimate (NA for intercepts).

"classes"

One row per class: class, share, count, n_assigned, mean_posterior, prior, prior_std_error, and for a Gaussian model the residual standard deviation sigma with sigma_std_error.

"membership"

One row per coefficient of the class membership model: the logit estimate against a reference class, with its standard error, test, interval and odds_ratio.

"group_classes"

Two-level fits (empty otherwise): one row per group class and class, with the probability of the class within the group class and group_share.

"fit"

One row: the family, nesting, class counts, numbers of observations and groups, log likelihood, number of parameters, aic, bic (on the rows under observation nesting, on the groups under group or two-level nesting), bic_rows, sabic, icl, entropy, group_entropy, smallest_share, convergence and replication.

"assignments"

One row per observation: row, the identifier, class, posterior and one probability_class_* column per class.

"groups"

Fits with id (empty otherwise): one row per group, with its number of rows, its class or group class and the posterior probabilities.

"fitted"

One row per observation: row, observed, fitted, fitted_modal, residual, class. An ordinal outcome is scored 1,...,C.

"starts"

One row per start: start, kind, log_likelihood, converged, iterations, stage ("screened" or "completed"), degenerate, selected.

"classification"

For the units assigned to each class, their mean posterior of every class: assigned, class, mean_posterior, n_assigned.

"recovery"

The assigned classes against known ones: one row per assigned class and truth value, with n and share. Needs data and truth (one column of data), and takes by = "class" (default) or "group_class". Not in "all".

Identifier columns that collide with output names use an id_ or cluster_ prefix, with a unique suffix if needed.

A growth mixture (mixture_regression() with random):

"coefficients"

One row per class and term of the growth curve, with standard error, test and interval.

"classes"

One row per class: share with its standard error and interval, expected_persons, assigned_persons, average_posterior, residual_sd.

"random"

Variances, standard deviations and correlations of the random effects, one row per class and parameter, with intervals on the log and Fisher scales.

"membership"

The coefficients of the class membership model.

"fit"

One row: class count, persons, observations, the random-effect structure, number of parameters, log likelihood, aic, bic, bic_rows, sabic, icl, entropy, smallest_share, convergence and replication. In a multilevel growth mixture bic is on the clusters and bic_persons on the persons.

"assignments"

One row per person: the identifier, class, probability and one posterior_* column per class.

"random_effects"

One row per person: the identifier, class and the predicted random effects.

"trajectories", "individual"

Each class's mean curve with its band (class, the time variable, estimate, std_error, conf_low, conf_high), and each person's curve (the identifier, the time variable, class, observed, class_mean, predicted). Both take time, the name of the numeric time variable.

"starts"

One row per start, as for a mixture regression.

"group_classes", "clusters"

Only in a multilevel growth mixture: its group classes and its clusters.

"recovery"

As for a mixture regression, without by. Not in "all".

An additive fit (multilpa() with family = "additive", "dispersion" or "additive_dispersion"):

"parameters"

Class means, between- and within-group variances and class weights: level, group_class, indicator, parameter, estimate, standard_error, statistic, p_value, p_adjusted, conf_low, conf_high. Variance intervals are formed on the log scale and weight intervals on the logit scale. Takes adjust ("none" by default).

"group_classes"

One row per group class: group_class, weight, count, n_assigned, mean_posterior and effective_groups, the number of perfectly classified groups that would estimate the weight as precisely (below 50, intervals warn).

"groups"

One row per group: the identifier, n, group_class, posterior and one probability_group_class_* column per group class.

"intercepts", "conditional_intercepts"

The predicted intercept of each group on each indicator (intercept_mean, intercept_variance): one row per group and indicator, and one row per group, indicator and group class.

"assignments"

One row per observation, with the group class of its group.

"classification"

For the groups assigned to each group class, their mean posterior of every group class.

"fit", "starts"

One row describing the fit; one row per start.

"recovery"

The assigned group classes against known ones. Needs data and truth. Not in "all".

A cross-level fit (multilpa(family = "restricted_cross_level") or "full_cross_level"):

"profiles"

The profiles, then the group classes' means of the group means: level, profile, indicator, mean, variance, prevalence.

"group_classes"

One row per group class: group_class, weight, count, n_assigned.

"composition"

The share of each profile within each group class (group_class, profile, share): model-implied for the full family, a posterior-weighted description for the restricted one.

"groups", "assignments"

One row per group, and one row per observation, with their classes and posterior probabilities.

"fit", "starts", "gaussian_diagnostics"

One row describing the fit; the record of the starts (for the restricted family, one row per part of the search); one row per Gaussian component.

The criteria of a cross-level fit come from a working likelihood and do not choose the number of group classes or the form; see multilpa().

A general transition fit, the lta() fit of class multilpa_lta that the extensions of the basic transition model listed in lta() return:

"transitions", "initial"

The transition and initial probabilities the model implies, averaged over the groups and the occasions they apply to. "transitions" has one row per group class, occasion (NA when the transitions do not differ by occasion) and ordered pair of profiles: group_class, occasion, from, to, probability, origin_expected_count, supported, estimated. "initial" has group_class, profile, probability.

"transition_coefficients", "initial_coefficients"

The same parameters as log odds, one row per coefficient, with standard error, test, interval and odds_ratio.

"second_order_transitions", "second_order_coefficients"

Only for order = 2.

"profiles", "covariances", "responses", "ordinal", "count_means"

The measurement model, each with an occasion column: profile means and variances, covariances (under covariance_model = "full"), and the categorical, ordinal and count models of fits with such indicators.

"group_classes"

One row per group class: group_class, weight, count.

"assignments", "posteriors", "entropy", "information_criteria"

As for the other transition fits, with the same arguments.

"fit", "starts", "gaussian_diagnostics"

One row describing the fit; one row per start; and, for continuous indicators, one row per Gaussian component.

profile is "profile_1", ... in "profiles", "responses" and the transition tables of a general transition fit, and the profile's number in its other tables.

Pooled imputations (pool_imputations()):

"estimates"

One row per pooled parameter: level, outcome, term, parameter, estimate, standard_error, statistic, p_value, p_adjusted, conf_low, conf_high, df, and the within and between variances with riv and fmi.

"imputations"

Each imputation's aligned estimates, one row per imputation and parameter.

"fits"

One row per imputation: imputation, log_likelihood, n_parameters, converged and the label orders used to align it.

Table arguments

data

One row per observation of the fit, in the fitted order; NULL uses the columns the fit carries. The standard errors of "profiles" and "responses" come from parameter_inference() on these data; a fit that cannot supply them gives NA with a message when data is omitted, and raises the condition when it is given.

scale

For "profiles": "raw" (default) or "standardized", each indicator's deviation from its grand mean in units of the observed population standard deviation (a weighted mean and spread, without zero-weight rows, for a weighted fit).

format

For the posterior tables and "sequences", "long" (default, one row per unit and class) or "wide" (one row per unit). For "information_criteria", "wide" (default, one row) or "long" (one row per criterion and convention).

level

For the classification tables of a profile, class or transition fit: "individuals", "groups" or "both"; NULL (default) is "both" for a fit with two or more group classes and "individuals" otherwise. For the other model families level is the confidence level of the intervals (default 0.95).

truth

For "assignments", column names of data holding known labels. The table then cross-tabulates the model's labels against them, one row per class and truth value: assignment (the label compared: group_class for a truth constant within every group of a fit with group classes, profile otherwise), class, truth, value, n and proportion (the share of units with that truth value assigned to that class). Excluded units appear under class = NA. Labels are arbitrary, so a truth value assigned mostly to a class with another label is relabelling, not misclassification.

by, adjust

For "residuals": by is "profile" (default, each profile separately) or "overall" (pooled over the profiles), and adjust is the multiplicity correction across the pairs: "BH" (default), "none" or another stats::p.adjust() method.

definitions

For "information_criteria" in long format, TRUE adds each criterion's formula and reference; FALSE (default) leaves them out.

estimated, stable

For "transitions" of a multilpa_transitions fit; NULL (default) keeps every row. estimated = TRUE keeps the rows estimated from observed occupancy and FALSE the others; stable = TRUE keeps the diagonal cells (staying) and FALSE the off-diagonal ones (moving).

cutoff, using, criterion and the tree arguments belong to the grid tables and are described with them.

Information criteria

With q free parameters, n the sample size and EN the entropy of the classification: deviance = -2L, aic = -2L + 2q, bic = -2L + q log(n), sabic = -2L + q log((n + 2) / 24), caic = -2L + q (log(n) + 1), awe = -2(L - EN) + 2q (1.5 + log(n)), icl = -2L + q log(n) + 2 EN, kic = -2L + 3(q + 1) (as tidyLPA computes it) and clc = -2L + 2 EN (on the entropy sum, so not comparable with tidyLPA's CLC on relative entropy). EN is the soft entropy of the complete-data classification, as in ICL, AWE and CLC; in a two-level model it is the group-class entropy plus each row's profile entropy within its group class.

Every criterion with a sample size is reported under two conventions, "groups" (n the number of groups) and "individuals" (n the number of rows), which coincide in a single-level model; use one consistently across candidates. A transition fit keeps one entropy per level instead, since its profiles form a chain within a person. Rows with no observed indicator, groups made only of such rows, and units of weight zero are in no sample size and no entropy.

Classification quality

The odds of correct classification of a class is (p / (1 - p)) / (r / (1 - r)), with p the average posterior in the assigned class and r the estimated class proportion: near one, the classification is no better than the class proportions; five is a conventional benchmark, not a test. It is NA when p is missing or zero or r is zero or one (so always for a single class), and Inf when p is one at an interior r. relative_entropy is 1 - entropy_sum / (n log K), with entropy_sum the level's own entropy, between zero and one, higher meaning sharper classification; NA for a level with one class. A fit without group classes reports individuals only.

Bivariate residuals

"residuals" checks, pair by pair, that the indicators are independent within a profile, weighting each observation by its posterior. Two Gaussian indicators (kind = "gaussian"): observed is the posterior-weighted residual correlation, expected the correlation the fitted covariance implies, and statistic the difference of their Fisher transforms times sqrt(effective_n - 3), referred to the normal distribution. Two categorical or ordinal indicators ("categorical"): statistic is the Pearson chi-square of the posterior-weighted two-way table against the model's, Latent GOLD's bivariate residual times its df = (R - 1)(C - 1), with observed and expected the two tables' Cramer's V; the reference ignores that the model's table is estimated from the same data and can be conservative. A mixed pair or a pair with a count indicator ("mixed", "count"): observed is the posterior-weighted correlation of the values (a categorical indicator entering as its category number), expected zero, and no test. p_adjusted applies adjust across the pairs with a p-value. A weighted fit reports the descriptive columns and no tests.

See also

as.data.frame() for the primary table, summary() for every table, diagnostics() for the classification tables with their checks, and the verbs get_checks(), get_entropy(), get_classification(), get_avepp(), get_residuals(), get_replication(), get_candidates(), get_best(), get_deltas(), get_knees() and get_tree().

Examples

fit <- multilpa(
  course_engagement,
  vars = c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read", "forum_post", "attendance"),
  id = "student", n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 2, n_starts = 4,
  seed = 1
)
get_results(fit)

get_results(fit, what = "entropy")

names(get_results(fit, what = "all"))

get_results(fit, what = "assignments", data = course_engagement,
